body:
We used an offline VM running a copy of our Agie Classic Cut 2S machine control. We imported direct CAMCraft jobs for 15, 40 and 80 mm stock. The control plotted the correct depths and rough offsets of 0.245, 0.260 and 0.266 mm, respectively. Each job passed FORMALCHECK with setup and option warnings. See #2999 for verification of the selected quality on the loaded work.

All controller runs were offline. No physical cut was made.

Port onto the ported #2955 is pushed. The head is `4a94c23ce`. It merges cleanly with `main`.

What the port did:
- It merged `9787bf79e` (the ported #2955, with `main`, #2984 and #3537) into the branch. No rebase and no force-push.
- It used the zero-step setup of #2984 as the frame. The old `jescript.rs` writer of this branch is not used.
- The measured table is now in `camcraft_post::agie_setup`. `PunchSetup20` writes the height into `ID_HEIGHT` of the piece and the work, and into `ID_POSPOSZ`. It refuses a thickness that is not in the table.
- The review text names the thickness and its four offsets.
- The corner check uses the measured rough offset of the thickness. All checks of #2984 and #2955 stay.
- A 20 mm job is byte for byte the same as before.

Gate: quick 343 of 343 steps green. Clippy on `camcraft-post` and `camcraft-app` is clean. The PR body has the pinning tests and the readings.

Owed by the author: a fresh offline control import of a 15, 40 and 80 mm job. The earlier control plots used the old writer of this branch. The import must show the height on the piece and the work, zero steps, and the measured offsets.

The PR also changes the `camcraft-mcp` skill row. The body has `Process change: yes`.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 4a94c23ce345aaf23dd4eede6dcab9bae51b95aa -->
Needs changes before merge. Two blocking findings remain.

This is a safety-tier review. I read the full diff, including the changes from #2955, against the current upstream rules.

What passed:
- The setup uses the selected height for the piece, work and stock Z position.
- The post refuses unsupported heights before it publishes files.
- The corner check uses the measured rough offset for the selected height.
- The 20 mm setup and review text match the reference. The desktop test also checks all three native files against the existing goldens.
- The process change has `Process change: yes`. The PR does not edit `PROCESS_VERSION`.

Local checks:

PR head: `4a94c23ce345aaf23dd4eede6dcab9bae51b95aa`.
Tested base: `upstream/main` at `47aa341ff8bc75e420ca8bc52ff2fa9159d4486f`.
Trial merge: `111b6ef3d8d2ba201593ec95823526f6fd362967`. Its first parent is the PR head.
All builds and tests ran locally, in the foreground. No GitHub runner ran.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | 344 steps accepted; 0 failed; 0 stalled; 30.6 minutes |
| `camcraft-post` lib | 106 passed |
| `camcraft-post` `agie_safe_setup` | 6 passed |
| `camcraft-app` lib | 303 passed |
| `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main` | 4 steps accepted; 3 light tests passed; 0 failed; 0 stalled; 12.3 minutes |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | 61 steps accepted; 0 failed gate steps; 0 stalled; 24.0 minutes |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |

heavy lanes green on 4a94c23ce345aaf23dd4eede6dcab9bae51b95aa. Base: `47aa341ff8bc75e420ca8bc52ff2fa9159d4486f`. Steps: 61; 0 failed; 0 stalled.
The heavy tests had 55 passes and two expected failures. The gate checked the registered assertions for #1950 and #2849. Both failed as expected. They are not test passes or new PR failures.

Extra suites run:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test agie_native`: 12 passed. I ran this again after the heavy gate.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_doc_drift`: 6 passed.
- From `crates/ui`, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib agie_post -- --test-threads=16`: 3 passed. These tests read `examples/agie` and check the native file goldens.
- The quick gate ran these suites by name: `mcp_wire_contour` (8 passed), `example_catalog` (39 passed), `example_catalog_adaptive` (1 passed), and `example_catalog_edge_work` (1 passed).
- The four catalog tests ignored in debug ran in the heavy gate.
- No STEP fixture or importer changed. The extra kernel importer suites do not apply.

Mutations:

I used source copies under `/tmp/review-2964-mutations`. The harness used the unchanged contour source and copied setup data definitions and lookup code. It used the PR's test functions. It did not change the PR or the review worktree.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Set the rough offset to zero | Red: the acute corner refusal test failed |
| Remove both emitted-seam clearance checks | Red: the rounded entry refusal test failed |
| Use the 20 mm rough offset at every height | Red: the corner test for the selected height failed |
| Bypass the measured-height selection | Red: the test for an unsupported height failed |
| Original source, before and after the mutations | Green: all 4 tests passed |

Goldens moved: none. No recorded NC file changed. I checked the new inline ISO expectation line by line.

Requested before merge:

1. **Class: incomplete control qualification — `docs/decisions/2954-agie-stock-heights.md:7` and `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md:38`.** Complete the acceptance checks for the current writer. The [author's port report](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2964#issuecomment-7109434846) states that the earlier height plots used the old writer. The [parent review](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2955#issuecomment-7109590359) also requires fresh checks of the two oblique jobs. Run fresh offline imports from this head for 15, 40 and 80 mm stock, and for `POLY20` and `SLOPE20`. Confirm both height fields and zero erosion steps after import. Then confirm the effective quality, measured offsets, retained side, entry and separation with FORMALCHECK and GRAFICHECK. Record the results for every case on this PR. This closes the acceptance class for both #2954 and the included #2953 changes. Local file tests do not complete the required control checks.

2. **Class: fixed height instructions — `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md:48`.** Step 3 always gives the 20 mm offsets: 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm. These values are wrong for 40 and 80 mm stock. Make every offset instruction use the table row for the selected stock height. Keep the verification steps consistent with that table and the exported review text.

Main advanced during the checks to `01e177bf5d1423fe2515ad0dc6947263ca0e6800` (#3395, outline text). It does not change the EDM files or review laws. A merge-tree check against that commit is clean. The test results above cover the stated trial merge and base; they do not cover the later addition.

Logs remain in `gate-logs/quick-20261123-180501`, `gate-logs/light-20261123-183746` and `gate-logs/heavy-20261123-185015`. The review worktree and branch remain for the next round.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
